These PRs remove the @[expose] from those files without defs or instances:

BTW, did Claude prepare the whole PRs, or did it write a metaprogram that identifies these files?

It wrote a script (just some grepping, no Lean metaprogramming)
The remaining PRs all pass CI.

Yury G. Kudryashov said:

I think that we can also remove @[expose] from files with Prop-valued instances only, right?

I can't find the info in the reference manual anymore (looks like the module system section has been entirely reworked), but I thought instances always exposed their body?

I'm running

$ git diff --word-diff upstream/master... | rg "\[[-+]" | rg -v "^\[-@\[expose\]-\]public section$"

on these locally, to double check that Claude has not been naughty.

Actually, I also handled those: #38477 has them all.
You can even ignore instance in your check, because they are exposed by default.

I went by Kim's methodology upstairs --- but also ignoring instances is even nicer, and finds over 1000 files overall. I also pushed those to the PR. It is fully auto-generated using a shell script (no need to trust AI)... if this is preferred, I can split it per directory (on Monday).
aha, so can this use the "verification of shell script operations in CI" feature that (i think) we now have?
In theory, yes: #38480 tries to do this.

In practice, the commits I generated are too complicated for the current CI infrastructure (the logs show several checks failing for what appears to be quoting-related issues). If a friendly soul would like to rewrite my three-line incantation into a single command that can be checked, be my guest :-)
Or perhaps the infra can be improved, @Bryan Gin-ge Chen?

Michael Rothgang said:

In theory, yes: #38480 tries to do this.

I verified post hoc that the changes were only as expected, so sent this to bors.

Ah, bors waits for the CI check that reverifies x: commits. That's unfortunate, I think we should turn that off as a blocker until such time as the reverifier is actually fit for purpose.

In the meantime, I propose we merge this one by hand rather than let it rot.
The PR went through - thanks for the fast review!
The verification script is rewritten to run the verification in separate worktrees and post better comments in mathlib-ci#26.
Here's a new sweep: #39388. I'm trying to write a linter that will flag these cases (this PR was made with it): #39387

Eric comments, re: the linter (#39387):

I think we have a choice to make here in Mathlib, between:

  1. files should prefer to use public section and @[expose]. In this case, this linter is a good thing.
  2. files should prefer to use @[expose] public section, and @[no_expose]. In this case, this linter is just encouraging users to create footguns.

I don't think were ready to declare 1 as the strategy yet, and so I would be opposed to this linter (and changes like #39388) landing in mathlib.

But I guess we already bit the bullet towards (1) with #38480, no?
...in which case, #39395 ?
(I've started a related thread about this in the reviewers stream)

Reviving this... did anything come out of that thread? I just put #39395 up-to-date. A recent development is lean4#14357, which allows a more elegant implementation of the superfluousExpose linter I had in #39387

I think it would be good to have this linter against unnecessary @[expose] section in mathlib. Though I could also imagine that this linter could be a bit annoying, because it might fire on empty or almost empty files that don't have any definition yet. Maybe it should only fire when there is at least one declaration in the file?
Won't that just 'force' you to start your sections without the @[expose], which is the conservative default we should encourage?
Using the new version of the linter, I made another pass on mathlib and updated #39388: there are 136 modules that can be stripped of @[expose] without any downstream consequence.
How many of these are leaf files? When you say "downstream", is that files downstream within mathlib, or also in downstream projects?
The sections themselves do not define anything that could be consumed, and thus are mechanically hideable, there are no 'possible' consumers
also see https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/39388#issuecomment-5108117997

I've sent this to radar.

One mild worry I have is that when new material is added to such sections, authors might not realize that it's unexposed.

Random thought: could we have slightly different types of background colour for sections of files that are exposed vs unexposed?
